page: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an arm64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra processor family, specifically utilizing the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. It features 8 shared virtual CPUs (vCPUs) operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, with 8 physical cores and a single thread per core configuration. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 160 GB NVMe SSD. The virtualization layer is managed via the QEMU hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across several standard workloads. Multi-core stress-ng CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core metrics fall within the average range, as do software compilation with Clang and ray tracing tests. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by Geekbench single-core and PassMark CPU scores. Cryptographic performance is supported by hardware-accelerated AES, though the PassMark CPU encryption test registers as weak. Memory bandwidth is average for small cached blocks at 560.18 GB/sec, but drops to 79.75 GB/sec for larger uncached reads.

The server demonstrates average throughput for database operations and static web serving, achieving 10.27 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 8.6 GB/sec in web serving benchmarks. Conversely, text processing, image processing, and large-scale decompression tasks show weaker performance. Large language model inference is highly constrained, with text generation on a small 135M model scoring in the poor category. Given its shared CPU allocation and ARM architecture, the cax31 offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources, such as web serving, basic database hosting, and software compilation.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an arm64 virtual server featuring 8 shared vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 1.95 GB per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating under the QEMU hypervisor, this instance delivers average multi-core performance in stress-ng and software compilation benchmarks, though its single-core metrics and memory bandwidth for uncached blocks are relatively weak. The server lacks dedicated GPU hardware and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for resource-dense, multi-threaded workloads that tolerate shared CPU allocation. The cax31 is best suited for static web serving, lightweight database operations, and basic CI/CD or software compilation tasks.
